date:

                05 SEP 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu conferred National Awards on teachers from across the country at a function held in New Delhi today (September 5, 2026) on Teachers’ Day.
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that education is the most effective means of realizing the ideal of equality of opportunity enshrined in our Constitution.  She said that the achievement of negligible primary school dropout rate, has been made possible through the efforts of teachers. She appreciated all the teachers for this national success.
The President said that school education forms the foundation of education system. While knowledge and skills can be acquired at any time, imparting lessons in good conduct during childhood proves far more effective. By diligently focusing on the intellectual, physical, and moral development of children in the early grades, our teachers can prepare future generations of excellent students and dutiful citizens.
The President underlined that many students come from economically disadvantaged families; some are first-generation learners; others transition from ordinary village schools to large city schools; some are naturally shy; some possess immense talent but lack self-confidence; and some are children with special needs. It is the special responsibility of teachers to instill confidence in them and uplift all such students who, for any reason, feel a sense of inadequacy.
The President said that academic excellence, skill development, and entrepreneurship hold immense importance in the country's development. Establishing India as the skill capital of the world, and transforming it into a knowledge superpower, is among our national priorities.
The President said that we are moving towards the goal of building a Viksit Bharat and this goal can be achieved only through a world-class education system. Our teachers breathe life into the education system. We must strive to ensure that not even a single student in our country is deprived of opportunities for quality education. She emphasised that our teachers should instill knowledge, inspiration, morality, and sensitivity in all students through their affection and dedication.

title: VICE PRESIDENT LAUNCHES INDIA VALVE REGISTRY AT INDIA VALVES 2026 IN CHENNAI
subtitle:
India Valve Registry to strengthen evidence-based cardiac care: Vice President

India must generate its own clinical evidence for better patient care: Vice President

Healthcare is a human right ,Medical advancements must be inclusive and accessible to all: Vice President

A Viksit Bharat must also be a Swasth Bharat: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today launched the India Valve Registry at India Valves 2026, a national academic meeting dedicated to advancing the treatment of valvular and structural heart diseases, in Chennai.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the India Valve Registry during the India Valves 2026 conference in Chennai.
He highlighted the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence to strengthen cardiac research, improve medical decision-making and enhance…
pic.twitter.com/1NLbaZy0E5
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 5, 2026
Addressing leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and medical experts from India and abroad, the Vice President said that the coming together of clinical expertise, scientific inquiry, innovation and collaboration represents an important step in the service of humanity.
He underlined that behind every medical procedure, clinical decision and scientific advancement is ultimately a human being, a patient who wishes to live longer, healthier and with dignity.
Highlighting the remarkable advances made in cardiovascular medicine, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan noted that while valvular and structural heart diseases remain an important and growing challenge, advances in medical science have transformed the way these conditions are treated.
He emphasised that every advancement in medical science brings with it a new responsibility to ensure that its benefits are inclusive and accessible to all. He said that healthcare is a human right and should be accessible to everyone.
The Vice President described the launch of the India Valve Registry as an important step in this direction. He said that a valve registry, by systematically recording information on patients undergoing heart valve interventions, their treatment and outcomes over time, can transform individual clinical experiences into collective medical knowledge.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence. He noted that several countries have developed national registries for advanced valve interventions and other cardiovascular procedures and welcomed efforts to establish such a collaborative initiative in India.
He said that such registries would help create “our country’s own data for our own countrymen” and would enable the medical community to better understand outcomes, identify challenges and gaps, learn from experience and improve patient care.
The Vice President highlighted India’s growing stature as a centre of medical expertise and innovation. Referring to India’s achievements during the COVID-19 pandemic, he said that the country not only developed vaccines for its own people but also supplied vaccines to around 100 countries, demonstrating India’s growing medical and technological capabilities.
“Our doctors, scientists and healthcare professionals have earned respect across the world. India has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in advanced medical treatment,” he said.
Referring to the national goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that a developed India must also be a Swasth Bharat.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for collective efforts to build a healthcare ecosystem in which innovation, technology and scientific progress are ultimately measured by their ability to improve human lives.
The event was attended by Tamil Nadu Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Thiru K. G. Arunraj; Senior Interventional Cardiologist, Apollo hospitals, Chennai, Dr. G. Sengottuvelu;  Chairman, Cardiac Sciences, Fortis Escorts Heart Institute, New Delhi, Dr Ashok Seth; Chairman, Interventional Cardiology, Medanta–The Medicity, Gurugram, Dr. Praveen Chandra, besides eminent cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers, scientists and members of the organising committee.
About India Valves 2026 & India Valve Registry
India Valves 2026 is a national academic meeting on valvular and structural heart disease, bringing together leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and healthcare professionals from across the country and abroad for scientific exchange, training and collaborative research.
The India Valve Registry is a collaborative multicentre initiative for systematic, secure and de-identified collection of real-world data on transcatheter valve interventions across India, aimed at strengthening India-specific clinical evidence and improving patient care.

Over the years, this institution has given generations of students the opportunity to learn, grow and make a difference: PM

From policy paralysis to policy dynamism, India has come a long way: PM

India's 7.8% growth amid global uncertainty reflects its economic strength: PM

Together, 140 crore Indians will make India both Viksit and Aatmanirbhar: PM

India is moving forward at a new pace; What once took decades is now happening in just a few years: PM

If Indians can lead the world's top companies, Indian companies can lead the world too, It is all possible: PM
date:

                05 SEP 2026 9:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated in centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) today. Addressing the gathering he noted that the occasion is historic for both the college and the nation's education sector as multiple generations have gathered together. “I pay tribute to the founder Shri Ram ji and bow to his vision,” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting the profound significance of this 100-year milestone for both the college and the nation's education sector, the Prime Minister paid tribute to founder Shri Ram ji and bowed to his enduring vision. “When an institution turns 100, it becomes an ocean of achievements and inspirations,” observed Shri Modi.
Tracing the college's magnificent evolution from a modest establishment in Daryaganj to a towering educational institution, the Prime Minister noted that it has shaped generations. He acknowledged the immense pride associated with the institution's name today. “Even today in DU, saying you are from SRCC is a flex in itself,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Praising the stellar legacy of the college, the Prime Minister acknowledged the SRCC alumni as original trailblazers who have elevated the institution globally across various fields. He recalled his personal experiences working with notable alumni like the late Arun Jaitley and Sanjeev Sanyal, observing that graduates have excelled as artists, politicians, and judges. “Meaning, the alumni of SRCC have made their mark in every field,” noted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the widespread nostalgia surrounding the current event, the Prime Minister observed that people are fondly remembering and revisiting his previous 2013 address at the college. He mentioned that the speech created a lasting wave whose positive impact remains completely intact even after 13 to 14 years. “Devoting myself wholeheartedly to the country is the inner passion that manifested in my words that day,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Contrasting past struggles with today's achievements, the Prime Minister emphasized that terrorism has been defeated, with armed forces confidently striking enemies in their own homes and peace restored from Jammu and Kashmir to the Northeast. He highlighted that the world now praises India's policy dynamism and its status as the fastest-growing major economy. “Achieving a 7.8 percent quarterly growth amidst the West Asia war and global trade hurdles demonstrates India's intrinsic capability,” asserted Shri Modi.
Presenting hard economic data to counter persistent critics, the Prime Minister detailed that between April and June, electricity production increased by 9 percent, while overall vehicle sales surged by over 20 percent, driven by a 20 percent growth in two-wheelers and nearly 30 percent in three-wheelers. He argued that an 8 percent increase in steel and cement consumption proves that construction, housing, and commercial activity are rapidly expanding. “Despite this, for the people who saw the glass as half-empty in 2013, their mindset remains exactly the same today,” noted Shri Modi.
Recounting his 2013 promise of Pro-People Good Governance (P2G2), the Prime Minister stated that his government permanently discarded the reactive approach of previous administrations. He cited the 12-year success of the Jan Dhan Yojana as a prime example, recalling that until March 2014, over 50 percent of India's 1.25 billion population lacked bank accounts, whereas the scheme has now integrated around 60 crore citizens. “Today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system, which has formed the foundation of India's Fintech revolution,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Defending the 'Make in India' initiative against early mockery, the Prime Minister celebrated its monumental success in transforming the nation from a massive importer to a leading exporter. He proudly shared that smartphone exports now exceed Rs 2.5 lakh crore, while domestic defense production has hit an all-time high of nearly Rs 2 lakh crore, turning 2013-14 defense exports of a mere Rs 600-700 crore into a massive Rs 40,000 crore industry today. “I am not a person who walks with small and easy goals; I set huge targets for the country and put my heart and soul into achieving them,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Expressing immense trust in the youth and the capability of 140 crore Indians, the Prime Minister laid out a bold vision for a self-reliant and fully developed India. He outlined ambitious future milestones, including becoming a superpower in agriculture exports, establishing an Indian space station, and eventually hosting the Olympic Games. “And these are not just talks, these are our firm resolutions,” asserted Shri Modi.
Transitioning from the lively campus life of tea at the Co-op, Crossroads, and the Business Conclave to the realities of the outside world, the Prime Minister warned students about cynical individuals who compulsively oppose national progress. He pointed out how these naysayers habitually questioned vital projects like the world's tallest Statue, High-Speed Trains, UPI, and the new Parliament building. “But India gave an answer: no one can stop India from doing what is necessary for the country,” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting the unprecedented speed of infrastructure and policy execution, the Prime Minister noted that projects which previously took decades are now being completed in just a few years. He cited that despite India's first electric train running in 1925, less than 30 percent of railway lines were electrified by 2014, whereas his government achieved nearly 100 percent electrification in just 12 years, alongside signing Free Trade Agreements with 40 countries covering leather, textiles, and processed foods. “This is creating a new sky of opportunities for the youth of India,” observed Shri Modi.
Shri Modi recalled his administration's resilient handling of severe modern crises like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war. “There is so much power in the blessings of the people of my country that every desire of those wishing ill upon India is falling flat,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Encouraging the ambitious spirit of the 21st-century youth, the Prime Minister celebrated their drive to build unicorns, innovate in drone technology, and create cutting-edge AI solutions. He urged them to dream even bigger than previous generations, challenging them to build global consulting, accounting, financial, and legal firms that can lead the world. “Today, Indians are leading the top companies of the world, so why can't companies built by Indians lead the world?” noted Shri Modi.
Drawing inspiration from the SRCC college crest, the Prime Minister beautifully compared the youth's journey to a ship advancing toward a guiding sun. He called upon everyone to navigate a new path of self-reliance where the courage, the dreams, and the ultimate victory belong entirely to India. “On the path to a Viksit Bharat, every rapidly rising step should be ours,” asserted Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet Shri Prahlad Joshi ji, DU Vice Chancellor Yogesh Singh ji, SRCC Principal Simrit Kaur ji, Ajay ji, Mallika ji, Rajat ji, all companions connected with SRCC, faculty, staff, SRCC alumni, and my young friends!
I am the sixth player. Today’s occasion is very historic for Shri Ram College of Commerce, and equally important for the country’s education world. Here, many generations who have been part of SRCC have gathered together. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you for this centenary celebration of SRCC. I respectfully pay tribute to its founder, Sir Shri Ram ji, and bow to his vision.
Friends,
When a person lives for 100 years, he is considered an ocean of experiences. And when an institution completes 100 years, it becomes an ocean of achievements and inspirations. In its 100‑year journey, SRCC has shaped generations, connecting them to a bright future. Those who came studied, and those who left went out as well‑shaped individuals. The journey of this college began in Daryaganj, in a small place, and today that small college has become a huge tree. A tree that has given shade to many generations, and enriched them with its coolness. Even today, in DU, when someone asks which college, saying SRCC itself is a flex in itself.
Friends,
The alumni of SRCC have also been very special. If I say in your language, the alumni here are the OGs, who carried SRCC’s name across the world, making their mark in different fields. Rajat ji mentioned a long list. And I too have had the opportunity to work with some of them. Our Arun Jaitley ji studied here. And I can say that perhaps there was never a meeting with him where he did not narrate some incident of SRCC. Sometimes I would get tired, because he would repeat the same incident again and again. In my team today, brother Sanjeev Sanyal also studied here. Many other companions are here too. And it is not that only people from the world of economics came out of here - many artists, leaders, lawyers, judges have also come from here. That is, SRCC people have created a stir in every field. They may not all be giants, but they certainly created a stir.
Friends,
For the past few days, this program has been much discussed. Especially people are remembering my 2013 address. People have listened to it again, read it again. It is possible that the new generation has also revisited it. That speech, I can say, became a wave, a movement. And even today, 13–14 years later, the impact of that gathering, that address, remains.
Friends,
Then, in your place, your seniors were sitting. And I was then a Chief Minister, but also a member of the country’s main opposition party. And perhaps people then expected that I would make long attacks on the central government of that time, shower accusations.
But friends,
Even while being in opposition, even while being a critic of the then government, I did not use that platform for that. I placed a vision, spoke positive things. Whatever I said then was my conviction. I have always lived those words, those dreams. I have always walked that path - dedicating myself wholeheartedly for the country, living with the spirit of serving the nation. That inner world of mine, that emotional universe, on that day in 2013, from this very platform, came out one by one in a garland of words. And I spoke at length. Then I asked the students if I should continue, and they loudly said, “Yes, continue.”
Friends,
That day I gave the example of a glass of water, and it was much discussed in the country. I explained the three perspectives of looking at a glass half‑filled with water. One, those who see the glass as half full of water. Second, those who see the glass as half empty. And third, those who see the glass as completely full - half with water and half with air.
Friends,
This was the time when the country was sunk in the swamp of despair. Even then I said that I do not see the glass as half, I do not see it as incomplete - I see the glass as completely full. Half with water, half with air. And at that time you all must have been in school, but today if you go on the internet and read the news of 2013 and around that period, you will realize what the situation was. And I urge the youth - just look once at that period of 2013 on the internet, the headlines around my speech then. Whether newspapers or TV channels, what were the headlines then? Let me give you a glimpse of those headlines. Now there is a gang that will cut my words into small pieces and put them in my account, so I warn beforehand that what I am telling you is what dominated the media in 2013, such as:
• Indian soldiers killed on the LoC - today’s generation may find it strange that such things happened, but they did.
• World Bank lowered GDP growth forecast.
• Current account deficit at an all‑time high.
• Inflation rate around ten percent.
• Industrial sector caught in recession.
• Helicopter deal bribery exposed.
• Bomb blasts in Hyderabad.
These were the headlines of that time. I am sure today’s students do not know all this. These things show what the condition of the country was then. Growth was on the floor and inflation was on the ceiling. Scams were at their peak and the corrupt roamed fearlessly. The economy was in bad shape, everywhere there was talk of policy paralysis. The world counted India among the “Fragile Five.” Terrorists were unchecked and Pakistan was uncontrollable. That is, then there was nothing but despair and frustration.
Friends,
That was the day when on every front the country was struggling, and this is today - today those spreading terrorism are subdued. If Pakistan does any nefarious act, India’s forces enter their home and strike. From Jammu & Kashmir to the North East, peace has increased. Maoist terror, Naxalism has been broken. The world that was then worried about policy paralysis in India, today talks about India’s policy dynamism. Then the world called India part of the Fragile Five, today the world sees India becoming the fastest‑growing major economy. Just in the past week, many positive news items have come about India’s economy. The 7.8 percent quarterly growth has boosted the nation’s enthusiasm, and in the same period a Japanese credit rating agency has upgraded India’s rating.
And friends,
This 7.8 percent growth has come at a time when war is going on in West Asia, when there have been many trade‑related obstacles. To achieve such growth at such a time shows India’s capability in itself.
Friends,
I know, you also know, those who were infamous for pushing India into the Fragile Five, they cannot digest these figures. But you all understand the numbers seriously. Between April and June, electricity production increased by 9 percent, vehicle sales grew by more than 20 percent. In that too, two‑wheelers grew by 20 percent, and three‑wheelers by nearly 30 percent. That means consumer demand is running, and commercial activity is strong. Growth in steel and cement consumption increased by 8 percent. That means construction, housing, infrastructure, and industrial activity are all rising. That means India is growing, and creating new employment opportunities too. Despite this, for those who saw the glass half empty in 2013, their thinking remains the same even today. For them the glass will always be half empty. When I speak of the glass, I am not speaking of anything being empty.
Friends,
In 2013, speaking here at SRCC, I also spoke of P2G2 - Pro‑People Good Governance. Those who ran governments for long had a style - wake up only when there is fire, dig a well only when there is drought. I spoke of changing this approach. And after forming government in 2014, we have shown this in action. Let me give you an example.
Friends,
Recently, the Jan Dhan Yojana completed 12 years. Today you are living in a completely different era of fintech, but those were also the days of 2013 when students from villages or small towns had to struggle a lot even to open savings bank accounts. At that time our population had crossed 1.25 billion, but by March 2014, more than 50 percent of the country’s population did not even have bank accounts. And those outside the banking system were mostly the poor, women, migrant laborers, students. That is why we brought the Jan Dhan scheme, and in the past 12 years, because of Jan Dhan Yojana, nearly 600 million new bank accounts have been opened. Today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system. This became the foundation of India’s fintech revolution.
Friends,
Now think also about those people who opposed even connecting millions of people to the banking system. In fact, such people enjoyed only when the glass was half full, so that the poor ordinary citizens kept circling around them. This “mai‑baap” culture they had continued for decades. But this is Modi - standing like a rock before those who liked the mai‑baap culture.
Friends,
There is an old saying: truth fears no fire. I have courage, and that is why I am reminding you of what I said that day, bringing my report card before you. I know that before the roar of truth, the echo of lies cannot stand.
Friends,
In that 2013 program itself, when I said that we must work on Made in India, the people of the old ecosystem of that time could not even understand it. They thought that in that era of despair, Made in India would not be possible at all! And those who grew up in that thinking still mock Made in India.
But friends,
Today you are seeing the brand value of Make in India. Let me explain with an example. Today every hand has a smartphone. The world’s biggest phone brands are making India their base. Made in India smartphones are reaching every corner of the world. In 2014, India imported most of its mobile phones. Today India exports mobile phones worth more than 2.5 lakh crore rupees.
Friends,
I am not a person who takes small and easy targets. I set big goals for the country, and I put my whole life into achieving them. Look at the defense sector. Earlier, most things for India’s armed forces were bought from abroad. As soon as I came, I told the defense people - make a negative list. First they made a list of 500 items, saying these we will not bring from outside. Then they made 1,000, then 3,000. Army, Navy, Air Force - many times even for a small piece of equipment they had to wait for months. We made a plan together with the armed forces, made lists of items, then told Indian companies to make all these. And today you see, the country’s defense manufacturing is at its all‑time high. Today India is producing defense equipment worth nearly 2 lakh crore rupees. In 2013–14, we exported defense equipment worth 600–700 crore rupees. Today this figure has reached nearly 40,000 crore rupees. And these achievements are possible because today a vibrant defense manufacturing ecosystem is being built in the country.
Friends,
I have trust in the country, trust in the country’s capability, trust in you youth. And on the basis of this trust I speak of a developed India. I am confident that we 1.4 billion Indians together will make our country developed and self‑reliant.
•  In the coming time, India will be a hub of manufacturing.
• In the coming time, Hindustan will be a hub of research and innovation.
• India will be a superpower of agricultural exports.
My young friends,
• India will have its own space station.
And you will also see the day when India will host an Olympics in such a way that the world will be left watching in awe.
And these are not just words, these are our resolutions. And to turn these resolutions into reality, continuous work is happening in the country.
Friends,
Right now your life is running in SRCC mode. Whether it is tea at the co‑op, discussions over cold coffee, last‑minute notes for exams, rushing for printouts, or the hard work put into Crossroads and the Business Conclave - you have made every moment here a memory of your life. But outside this campus, a new world awaits you. You will meet two kinds of people. One, those who positively transform the power of society into the power of the nation. The second species are those who, whenever any work begins, become the “angry uncle.” Their favorite job is to oppose everything. Their permanent dialogue is: “What is the need for this? What is the need for this?” That is the permanent line of every such uncle. When we were building the world’s tallest statue, these uncles tightened their belts and said, “What is the need for this?” When we started work on the high‑speed train, they again said, “What is the need for this?” When we brought UPI, these same people said, “Why UPI? What is the need for UPI?” When we spoke of making chips, again they said, “What is the need for this?” When we built the new Parliament building, they said, “What is the need for this?” When we built a memorial for our brave military commanders who gave the supreme sacrifice for the nation, again they came out saying, “What was the need for this?” But India has answered all such uncles - whatever is necessary for the country, no one can stop India from doing it.
Friends,
Today India is moving forward with a different temperament. Work that earlier took decades is now happening within just a few years. Let me give you another example with full facts. India’s first electric train ran in 1925. Your college started in 1926, but the train ran in 1925. After that, until 2014 - that is, 90 years - less than 30 percent of railway lines were electrified. In just 12 years, we have shown nearly 100 percent electrification of railway lines.
Friends,
This speed in India’s policy decisions is being seen and understood by the rest of the world. That is why they are increasing their partnerships with India. In the past decade, trade agreements and free trade agreements have been signed with nearly 40 countries. Because of this, new markets are opening for leather, textiles, fruits and vegetables, our processed food, shrimp, and many other products. Who better than you knows what it means when new markets open, when tariffs are reduced for India’s goods and services. This is creating a new sky of opportunities for India’s youth.
Friends,
Today, compared to 2013, the country is far more secure economically and socially. But seeing this, some people’s restlessness and frustration are increasing. You must have heard my speech on 15th August. For such people, I gave a dose of homeopathy from the Red Fort - a small homeopathy pill. And you know, they say the nature of homeopathy is that when you start the medicine, at first the illness flares up even more. That is the nature of homeopathy. So from the Red Fort I gave a homeopathy pill - “mental Naxal.” This mental Naxal treatment, as I said, first flares up the illness for some time, and then begins the cure. In the same way, as soon as I gave the mental Naxal pill, all the mental Naxals started coming out. And those who are promoting this illness, now the public is seeing their true colors too.
Friends,
I have said so many things, some people may think - oh, what is the big deal, it was a country of 1.4 billion, it was easy, what new did Modi do? But was it really so easy? Let me take you back once again to the old days. Remember when you were in school. In 2013, when the disaster struck Kedarnath, the entire government was shaken. They did not know what to do, how to do it. In 2008, when the banking crisis came, the government of that time tried to hide behind that crisis until 2014, not daring to even touch it. India’s entire banking system was brought to the brink of collapse. In 2008 itself, when the horrific terrorist attack happened in Mumbai, the government then came under external pressure, but did not even show the courage to teach Pakistan a lesson.
Friends,
In the past 12 years, many disasters have struck the country, we have faced huge cyclones, but the nation has faced them strongly. In the past 6 years, very big crises have come. First the pandemic of corona, which shut down the whole world. Then the war broke out between Russia and Ukraine. After that, the era began of weaponizing trade and supply chains. Then came the crisis in West Asia. Every time it was said, now India will not survive. And those who are my “special admirers” were happy thinking - now Modi is trapped, now Modi will fall, now he will be crushed. But the blessings of my country’s people have such strength, such strength, that every wish of those who wanted India’s downfall has been left unfulfilled.
Friends,
Now in the 21st century, a world of new opportunities is before us. I am happy that you are ambitious, because ambition cannot be taught from a textbook. Ambition comes from the environment that inspires you to dream big. Today our young companions say - if I do something, I will start a startup, if I build a company, I will make it a unicorn. I will join sectors like space and drones, I will do something big. I will build cutting‑edge AI solutions, I will innovate in agriculture. Thirteen years ago, your seniors could not even dream such dreams. But today you are dreaming them, because in today’s India an ecosystem has been built to support those dreams.
Friends,
Now is the time to set big goals and achieve them. Just recently from the Red Fort I said some things. I want to repeat them among you. Take a pledge - why can’t India have global consulting firms? Why can’t our accounting firms, our legal firms, our financial firms become global leaders? We proudly say that today Indians are leading the world’s top companies. If Indians are leading the world’s top companies, then why can’t companies created by Indians lead the world?
Friends,
All this is possible. For this you have both networks and knowledge.
Friends,
Our inspiration, your inspiration, is also the SRCC college crest. It has two beautiful symbols. One is the rising sun, and the other is the ship moving forward in the sea. The sun, which shows direction, and the ship, which moves forward in that direction. We must walk on such new paths, where the sun is ours, the sea is ours. The boat is ours, the sailor is ours. The courage to write victory on the waves is ours. The flight is ours, the sky is ours. The spirit to face strong winds is ours. The dream is ours, the resolve is ours, the banner of self‑reliant India is ours. On the path of developed India, every step rising swiftly is ours. Once again, on this special occasion, I extend my many best wishes to all connected with SRCC.
Vande Mataram.

title: Coal India Output and Dispatch Set to Accelerate as Monsoon Effect Wanes
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As the intense rains over coal command regions show clear signs of easing, coal production and supplies at Coal India Limited (CIL) are gathering pace and are set to improve further from here on. Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and August, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. During April–August of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.90 million Tonnes (MT) of coal, 6.70% higher than the 302.60 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year.
The easing rainfall is already bringing relief on the ground. Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet after prolonged rain exposure are now drying out, making freshly mined coal free-flowing and considerably easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs). Coal seams at lower mine horizons that had been submerged are being restored to production through augmented pumping, while repair of internal haul roads is progressing in full swing.
Mines across CIL are consequently stepping up preparations to return to full operational pace, with the focus firmly on ensuring that production and coal movement pick up quickly as ground conditions continue to improve. While average daily coal production during the rain-affected first three days of September stood at around 1.36 MT per day, it rose to approximately 1.7 MT per day  on 04.09.2026, even with just a single day's respite from rain.
Overburden Removal (OBR) – a key indicator of coal bed exposure and future production readiness – has also started gaining momentum. Average daily OBR during the first three days of September stood at 2.5 Million Cubic Metres, improving to 4.1 Million Cubic Metres on 04.09.2026. This improvement in OB removal, together with drying mine conditions, is expected to lend further impetus to production and supplies in the days ahead.
CIL supplied 60.60 MT of coal in August FY 2026–27, registering a 5.50% increase over supplies in August last year. Supplies to the power sector in August 2026 also rose 4.5% to 48.46 MT, compared to August 2025. CIL continues to hold a stock cushion of 76 MT of coal at its pitheads, along with 46 MT of ready-to-mine coal exposure. Average daily dispatch to the power sector, at around 1.35 MT over the first three days of September, has since improved to 1.5 MT on 4th September. Driven by the coal fraternity's commitment to the larger national cause, dispatch to evacuation points is set to see a marked step-up in the coming days through enhanced production and transportation.
With drier conditions setting in, geo-technical concerns around dump and bench stability – and the associated safety risks that intensify during rain – stand considerably reduced, allowing the workforce to operate unhindered at ground zero. To ensure a streamlined flow of coal, CIL subsidiaries have used the lean period to augment their CHP-Silo mechanisms, and with the dry season approaching, rail tracks at loading points and yards are being cleared. Companies such as NCL and SECL have also created additional crushing capacity that will prove valuable in the near term.
The spell of incessant rain has largely passed, and any intermittent showers going forward are not expected to materially affect mining operations.
Alternate modes offered to augment supplies
In view of the availability of adequate coal stock at various sources across the subsidiary companies of Coal India Limited (CIL), and with a view to augmenting coal supplies to the power sector, CIL has offered power plants having Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) with Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries to lift additional quantities of coal, including quantities over and above the applicable Annual Contracted Quantities, through road mode, in addition to the existing rail mode, as per the applicable provisions of their respective Fuel Supply Agreements.
With dry spells setting in, loading is expected to pick up further over the coming days. Close monitoring is being maintained to sustain this trend.

title: Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects: Ministry clarifies position on applications
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 11:22AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Reference is drawn to reports appearing in a section of the press suggesting that the ₹37,500 crore Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects has not attracted any applications. The Ministry of Coal wishes to place the correct facts on record and clarify that such reports are premature and do not reflect the status of the Scheme or the application process.
The Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects was approved by the Union Cabinet on 13 May 2026 with a total financial outlay of ₹37,500 crore. The Scheme is aimed at accelerating the development of coal and lignite gasification in the country and promoting the conversion of domestic coal and lignite into higher-value products, including syngas, methanol, ammonia and urea. By facilitating greater utilisation of domestic resources for production of such value-added products, the Scheme seeks to reduce dependence on imported feedstock and strengthen India’s energy and economic security.
Following approval of the Scheme, the Ministry of Coal undertook sustained outreach and stakeholder engagement to encourage participation from potential project developers. Roadshows were organised in New Delhi on 28 May 2026, Hyderabad on 11 June 2026 and Mumbai on 18 June 2026. These events brought together representatives from State Governments, public and private sector companies, technology providers, investors, financial institutions and other stakeholders. The events were attended by the Union Minister of Coal and Mines and senior officials of the Ministry, reflecting the Government’s emphasis on building awareness and facilitating industry participation in the Scheme.
The Request for Proposal under the Scheme was issued on 7 July 2026, following which the online portal for submission of applications was launched. To facilitate greater clarity and ensure that prospective applicants had an opportunity to seek clarifications, a pre-application conference was held on 20 July 2026. During the conference, prospective applicants raised queries and sought clarifications relating to various provisions of the Scheme, eligibility requirements and the application process. The Ministry has also continued to engage with interested stakeholders to facilitate their participation.
The first-round deadline for submission of applications is 7 September 2026. Accordingly, the number of applications received in the first round cannot be assessed or stated conclusively until the application window closes. Any conclusion that the Scheme has received no applications, while the first application window is still open, is therefore premature and does not represent the actual position.
Further, based on discussions with stakeholders, the Ministry has been informed that Talcher Fertilisers Limited (TFL) and NTPC Limited have already submitted their respective applications through the online portal. This itself demonstrates that the assertion that the Scheme has received “no takers” is factually incorrect. The Ministry is also in communication with other prospective applicants who are at various stages of project preparation and application finalisation.
Given the significant scale and complexity of the projects envisaged under the Scheme, prospective applicants are required to undertake substantial preparatory work, including preparation of Pre-Feasibility Reports, assessment of technology options, identification of coal/lignite and other feedstock arrangements, evaluation of project economics and preparation of detailed project proposals. It is therefore expected that additional applicants may finalise and submit their proposals as the deadline approaches.
Importantly, the Scheme has been structured to provide industry with multiple opportunities to participate. Application rounds will operate on a rolling basis. Upon closure of the application window for one round, the subsequent round will open from the very next day and remain open for a period of two months. This ensures that companies that may require additional time to complete project preparation are not excluded merely because they are unable to participate in an earlier round. The rolling-round mechanism has been deliberately incorporated in view of the substantial preparation and investment requirements associated with large-scale coal/lignite gasification projects.
The Ministry remains confident of strong industry participation in the Scheme. The initiative is expected to catalyse investments of approximately ₹2.5 lakh crore to ₹3 lakh crore across nearly 25 projects and generate around 50,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities. The Scheme will also contribute significantly towards the Government’s broader objective of achieving 100 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity by 2030.
The Ministry reiterates that the Scheme is at an early stage of implementation and that the first application window remains open until 7 September 2026 and therefore, it is not appropriate to characterise the Scheme as having received “no takers” at an interim stage. Its success and level of participation should be assessed after completion of the prescribed application process and subsequent rounds, rather than on the basis of premature assessments.
The Ministry remains confident that the Scheme will receive sustained industry participation and will provide a significant impetus to the development of coal and lignite gasification in India.

title: National Biodiversity Authority Crosses ₹200-Crore Milestone in ABS Disbursement
subtitle: ₹8.23 crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing proceeds to be disbursed to States and UTs from utilisation of four key vegetable crops
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

                05 SEP 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has crossed a significant milestone in the implementation of India’s Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) framework, with cumulative ABS disbursements exceeding ₹200 crore. As part of this continuing effort, the NBA has sanctioned ₹8.23 crore in ABS proceeds to 27 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 5 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), arising from the access and utilisation of biological resources associated with Bitter Gourd (Momordica charantia), Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Chilli (Capsicum annuum) and Onion (Allium cepa).
The ABS proceeds were realised from seed companies M/s Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. in connection with access to these biological resources for research and commercial utilisation.
The biological resources had been accessed through the open market or through traders and hence could not be traced to specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Accordingly, in accordance with the modality recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority, the beneficiary share is being distributed among the SBBs/UTBCs of the States and Union Territories where the respective crops are cultivated.
The distribution is based on the area under cultivation, as published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. This approach enables the ABS proceeds to be channelled towards States and Union Territories associated with the cultivation of the respective biological resources, where direct identification of the individual providers or source communities is not possible.
Among the States and UTs receiving the ABS proceeds, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra emerge as the largest cumulative recipients across the four crops. Madhya Pradesh's share is supported by its cultivation of Bitter Gourd, Chilli and Onion, while Maharashtra's position is primarily attributed to its significant share of India's Onion cultivation area, accounting for more than 49 per cent. content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will chair the 28th meeting of the Western Zonal Council in Panaji, the capital of Goa, on Monday, September 7, 2026. The Western Zonal Council comprises the States of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra, and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Five Zonal Councils, including the Western Zonal Council, have been established under Sections 15 to 22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah is the Chairman of the Western Zonal Council, while the Chief Minister of Goa is its Vice-Chairman. From among the member States, the Chief Minister of one State serves as the Vice-
Chairman of the Council on a rotational basis every year. The meeting is being organised by the Inter-State Council Secretariat, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, and is being hosted by the Government of Goa. The Zonal Council comprises the Chief Ministers of each State in the Western region and two senior Ministers from each State as members. Senior officers from the Government of India and the State Governments/Union Territory will also participate in the meeting of the Council.
The Zonal Council has also constituted a Standing Committee at the level of Chief Secretaries. The issues proposed by the States are first placed before the Standing Committee of the Zonal Council for discussion. After deliberation, the issues that remain unresolved are then placed before the meeting of the Zonal Council for consideration.
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has envisioned TEAM BHARAT for the country based on the principle of cooperative federalism, and the Zonal Councils are making an important contribution in this direction. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has emphasised the need to harness the potential of cooperative and competitive federalism to achieve all-round development.
With the spirit that strong States make a strong nation, the Zonal Councils provide a structured mechanism for dialogue and discussion on issues affecting two or more States, or the Centre and the States together, and serve as a platform for enhancing mutual cooperation through this process.
The role of the Zonal Councils is advisory; however, over the past few years, these Councils have emerged as an important factor in fostering healthy bonds of mutual understanding and cooperation across various sectors.
With the cooperation of all State Governments, Central Ministries and Departments, a total of 70 meetings of various Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees have been held over the past 12 years (from June 2014 to date).
The Councils also discuss broad issues of national importance, including the expeditious investigation of cases of rape against women and children and the implementation of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) for their speedy disposal; implementation of the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112); issues related to food safety standards; provision of brick-and-mortar banking facilities within a designated radius of every village; and issues relating to nutrition, education, health, power sector reforms, urban planning, strengthening the cooperative system, cybercrime and digital infrastructure, among others.

ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS in PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today called
for continued effort to make service rules more responsive to employees and their families.
Welcoming the ‘CSS Shield’ initiative of the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum, Dr Jitendra Singh said, such collective efforts can create a new culture of standing by families in times of sudden loss. Speaking at the launch of the initiative, he said that the mechanism is not difficult to implement; what matters is the collective will and willingness to contribute. He said that when colleagues come together as one family to support a bereaved family, it sends a meaningful message beyond the organisation itself.
The Minister was speaking at an event organised by the Central Secretariat Service Forum for the launch of ‘CSS Shield’, a mutual support initiative for the bereaved families of CSS officers. The programme was attended by office-bearers and members of the CSS Forum, serving CSS officers and colleagues, besides family members of late Shri Mohan Chandra Bhatt and late Shri Rajendra Chandra. Dr. Jitendra Singh presented financial assistance to the families of the two deceased officers as part of the initiative.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the initiative is in keeping with the larger effort of the Personnel Ministry to make government service systems more responsive to the needs of employees and their families. He said that several service-related provisions have been changed in recent years to reflect contemporary requirements and that the Government remains open to introducing new provisions or modifying existing rules wherever this can make the system more responsive.
Referring to the approach of the Government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that there is continuous encouragement to review rules and procedures and make necessary changes wherever existing arrangements can be improved. He said that the objective is to ensure that government systems remain sensitive and responsive to the needs of employees and their families.
The Minister also suggested that the initiative could acquire a wider dimension as its participation and corpus grow. He said that scholarships for the children of deceased CSS officers could also be considered as part of the support extended through the initiative, providing assistance to families beyond the immediate period of loss.
The CSS Shield initiative has been conceived around the principle of “Contribute for Family, Support with Dignity”, with the objective of providing collective financial support to the bereaved families of CSS officers. The initiative seeks to ensure a more structured and dependable mechanism through which members of the service community can stand by the families of their colleagues.
Speaking about the evolution of the initiative, representatives of the CSS Forum said that the Forum had been supporting the families of deceased CSS officers through voluntary contributions even before the formal launch of CSS Shield. The experience during the COVID-19 period, when a number of CSS officers lost their lives, further strengthened the need for a structured mechanism of mutual support.
The Forum said that, since 2020, CSS officers have collectively contributed around ₹1.30 crore towards financial assistance for the families of approximately 65–70 deceased officers. The CSS Shield initiative has now been formalised to bring greater consistency and predictability to this support.
Under the new initiative, the Forum seeks to provide at least ₹15 lakh to a bereaved family, while its larger objective is to progressively enhance the assistance as participation increases. With the participation of the approximately 13,000 members of the Central Secretariat Service, the Forum envisages taking the support substantially higher in the future.
The programme also paid tribute to late Shri Mohan Chandra Bhatt and late Shri Rajendra Chandra, recalling their contribution and service. Shri Bhatt had served in different capacities in the Central Secretariat Service and other government organisations, while Shri Rajendra Chandra had served for around two decades in the Administration Division of the Department of Revenue.
The launch of CSS Shield reaffirmed the CSS Forum’s commitment to standing with its members and their families in difficult times and strengthening the spirit of “Together We Serve, Together We Support.”

title: CSIR-CRRI Conducts Specialized Training for PWD Delhi Engineers on CAQM Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CRRI)
organized a specialized training program for engineers of the Public Works Department (PWD), Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD), at the NDMC Convention Centre. The program centered on the
implementation
of the
Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Standard Framework for the paving and greening of urban roads
across the National Capital Territory.
The inaugural ceremony commenced with a traditional lamp lighting and formal welcome of dignitaries. The Director of CRRI Dr.Ch.Ravi Sekhar delivered the inaugural address alongside addresses by the Sh.Naveen Bansal, Engineer-in-Chief (EinC), PWD, and Sh. Ravi Jha, Special Secretary-2, PWD. The address underscored the critical role of scientific road design, environmental mitigation, and standard paving techniques in curbing road dust and improving Delhi's overall air quality.
The comprehensive one-day training schedule covered technical and field-level planning modules led by CRRI domain experts and Scientists including
Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Dr.Sampath Kumar, Dr. K. Ravinder, Dr. E. Madhu, Dr. Mukti Advani, Dr. Minal Chandra, Dr. Chintaman Bari and Dr. Nischal Gupta
.
Framework Background & Principles:
In-depth orientation on the background of paving and greening guidelines in the NCR region, principles of urban space standards, and road network planning aligned with IRC guidelines to enhance environment and safety.
Carriageway Design & Data Formats:
Technical guidance on carriageway standards for various categories of urban roads along with standard data collection formats.
Transit & Non-Motorized Transport (NMT):
Engineering benchmarks for public transport facility design, alongside dedicated standards for pedestrian walkways and non-motorized transport.
Safety & Infrastructure Integration:
Technical sessions detailing road signs and markings, as well as seamless integration of essential urban utilities—including drainage, electric utilities, telecom networks, bus stops, and gas fuel stations.
The session concluded with an interactive discussion between CRRI Scientists and participating PWD engineers to outline the operational roadmap and way forward for field-level implementation across the capital's road network.

title: DSIR-CRTDH on Affordable Healthcare at IIT Kharagpur enters sustainable phase, strengthens lab-to-market translation and last-mile healthcare delivery
subtitle:
Secretary, DSIR and Director General, CSIR, Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, inaugurates sustainable phase of the Hub

Hub has facilitated over 20 technology transfers and supported commercialisation of affordable medical technologies

Rural health workers trained under the Hub take affordable diagnostic technologies to underserved communities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sustainable Phase of the Common Research and Technology Development Hub (CRTDH) on Affordable Healthcare at IIT Kharagpur was inaugurated today by Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), at the Ben Gupta Auditorium, IIT Kharagpur.
Established in 2019 under the CRTDH Scheme of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India, the CRTDH on Affordable Healthcare has successfully completed its initial grant-supported phase and has transitioned into a sustainable phase. The Hub is now operating as a self-sustaining national facility for affordable healthcare technology development and translation, meeting its operational costs through user fees, industry sponsorships and translational partnerships, while continuing to provide infrastructure and technical support to innovators. The facility will continue to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure, technical expertise, and technology development support to MSMEs, startups, innovators, and other stakeholders. The transition of the CRTDH to a self-sustaining model marks an important milestone in strengthening industry–academia collaboration, technology translation, and innovation-led healthcare solutions, while ensuring the continued availability of shared research and technology development infrastructure. The programme was organised as part of the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur.
Chief guest of the event, Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, DSIR and DG, CSIR, in her address emphasised the role of DSIR and the network of CRTDHs in enabling MSMEs, start-ups and individual innovators to strengthen indigenous capability in medical technology. She said that the continued functioning of a CRTDH beyond the period of DSIR support demonstrates the intended outcome of the programme i.e. to serve industry and innovators in a self-sustaining mode. She emphasised that wider utilisation of these facilities would contribute to strengthening the country's indigenous technological capabilities, advancing self-reliance in medical device technologies, and supporting the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India for Viksit Bharat 2047.
On this occasion, Dr. (Mrs.) Kalaiselvi visited the CRTDH wet and dry laboratories and the THRIVE Centre along with Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, (Principal Investigator, CRTDH) and DSIR officials. Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi planted a sapling on the IIT Kharagpur campus, symbolising the beginning of the sustainable phase of the DSIR-CRTDH at IIT Kharagpur and reaffirming the commitment towards its continued growth, sustainability, and long-term contribution to innovation and technology development.
Presenting the journey of the Hub from 2019 to 2026, Prof. Suman Chakraborty highlighted the importance of frugal innovation in addressing the constraints faced in real-world healthcare delivery. He stated that designing technologies for use in settings without sophisticated infrastructure and by frontline health workers requires engineering solutions that are robust and accessible. Operating from a 5,000-square-foot facility, the CRTDH has facilitated over 20 technology transfers, many already commercialised, and has partnered with clinical and non-governmental organisations to establish rural health units to support the deployment of affordable healthcare technologies through rural health units.
During the MSME Voices session, enterprises mentored by the CRTDH shared their experiences while translating laboratory prototypes into commercial products. The participating enterprises were felicitated by the Chief Guest and the Director, IIT Kharagpur. Fifteen frontline health workers from remote villages, including the Sundarbans and Birbhum, shared their experiences of deploying affordable diagnostic technologies at the community level. Trained and certified under the Hub’s skilling programmes, in line with the objectives of Skill India, these health workers are now operating rural health units alongside the health delivery structures under the National Health Mission. Through these units, the trained health workers support screening, referral and follow-up services for communities where access to diagnostic facilities remains limited or intermittent.
Dr. Vipin Shukla, Scientist ‘G’ and Head of the CRTDH Scheme of DSIR, whose guidance has been instrumental in the development of the CRTDH initiative, was also acknowledged on the occasion. Dr. Ranjeet Bairwa, Scientist ‘F’ and Member Secretary – CRTDH, DSIR, and Dr. Kailash Petkar, Scientist ‘D’, DSIR, who closely monitored the implementation of the project, were also present during the event and participated in the proceedings. Continued association of the DSIR-CRTDH team with the project was duly acknowledged, followed by a screening of the CRTDH film.
The proceedings highlighted the convergence of frugal technology, local skilling and public health delivery as an important pathway for achieving the objectives of Viksit Bharat to the last mile. The initiative demonstrates how self-reliance in medical devices, employment opportunities for rural youth and equitable access to healthcare can be addressed through an integrated innovation and delivery ecosystem. At the end, the DSIR officials were felicitated by the Director, IIT, Kharagpur. The proceedings were coordinated by Mr. Sohom Banerjee, Project Manager, CRTDH, IIT Kharagpur.
Approximately 200 participants attended the program, including Senior Officers of DSIR, delegates from chambers of commerce and MSME associations, officials of Government MSME development institutions, MSMEs, start-ups, innovators, clinical partners, rural health workers, faculties, researchers, and students of the Institute. Technologies developed at the CRTDH and products commercialised by partner enterprises were exhibited during the event, providing an opportunity for participants to interact with the innovators.

title: NCSC Seeks Time Bound Response Over Complaint Regarding Denial Of Reservation Benefits To SC Candidates In The Recruitment Process For Lecturer Posts
subtitle:
Notice Issued To Chief Secretary Of Punjab Government, Response Sought Within Seven Days

NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana describes ‘denial of reservation benefits to SC candidates in the recruitment process a very serious matter’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Exercising the powers conferred under Article 338 of the Constitution of India, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) has ordered inquiry into the matter connected to a representation from Shri Tarun Chugh, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) wherein he has alleged non-implementation of the reservation policy in the recruitment of Lecturers in the Punjab Education Department.
The representation complains that Scheduled Caste candidates have been denied the benefits of reservation in the recruitment process for 1,013 Lecturer posts notified by the Punjab Education Department.
In this regard, a notice has been issued to the Chief Secretary of the Punjab Government, directing him to submit to the Commission, within seven days of receipt of the notice, the facts of the case, the action taken on the allegations, and all related records (including the recruitment notification and the reservation roster).
It is alleged that in several subjects (Punjabi, Commerce, Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography, etc.), the reservation rules and the prescribed roster system have not been properly followed.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes has also clarified that if a response is not received within the stipulated time limit, it may, under Article 338 of the Constitution, exercise the powers of a civil court and issue summons for personal appearance.
The Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Shri Kishor Makwana, stated that the denial of reservation benefits to Scheduled Caste candidates in the recruitment process for Lecturer posts is a very serious matter.
He said that the Commission is committed to protecting the constitutional rights of Scheduled Castes and to ensuring strict compliance with reservation provisions in government services. The Commission will take all necessary steps in accordance with the law to ensure justice.

title: Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0
subtitle: Strengthening Business Resilience through Timely Credit Support
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 SEP 2026 10:27AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The ECLGS 5.0 provides targeted credit guarantee support to businesses affected by external disruptions. Implemented by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company, the scheme enables eligible lending institutions to extend additional working capital with reduced credit risk. It supports MSMEs, eligible non-MSME businesses and scheduled passenger airlines through government-backed guarantees. Building on the earlier phases of ECLGS introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic, the scheme strengthens access to institutional credit while supporting business continuity. Extensive outreach, digital access through the Jan Samarth Portal and participation of banks and financial institutions have expanded its reach. By improving liquidity, preserving employment and strengthening supply chains, ECLGS 5.0 contributes to business resilience and sustained economic growth during periods of global uncertainty.
Supporting Enterprises During External Economic Shocks
India remains committed to sustaining economic growth, safeguarding livelihoods and ensuring uninterrupted business operations amid evolving geopolitical developments. Such developments can affect supply chains, increase logistics costs and create liquidity pressures for businesses across sectors. To address these challenges, the Government approved
the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 on 5th May 2026
.
The scheme is implemented by the
National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC
). It provides
government-backed credit guarantees
to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) for extending
additional working capital to eligible business borrowers
.
It aims to facilitate an additional credit flow of up to ₹2.55 lakh crore.
The scheme
supports uninterrupted domestic production and resilient supply chains
. It also helps businesses preserve employment and sustain economic activity during external disruptions. Moreover, enhanced liquidity enables enterprises to meet short-term operational and financial commitments.
Evolution of ECLGS
The
ECLGS
was launched in
2020
under the
Aatmanirbhar Bharat Package
. The scheme aimed to help businesses overcome financial stress caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. It enabled MLIs to extend additional credit with 100% Government-backed guarantee support. ECLGS has evolved through successive phases to address the changing needs of different sectors.
ECLGS 1.0
covered
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), business enterprises, Mudra borrowers and individual business loans
. Borrowers with outstanding loans not exceeding ₹50 crore and days past due upto 60 days as on 29 February 2020 were eligible.
ECLGS 2.0
expanded coverage to
26 stressed sectors
identified by the Kamath Committee and the healthcare sector. It covered borrowers with outstanding loans above ₹50 crore and up to ₹500 crore with days past due upto 60 days as on 29.02.2020.
ECLGS 3.0
extended support to the
hospitality, travel & tourism, leisure & sporting and civil aviation sectors.
Eligible borrowers had credit facilities with lending institutions and up to 60 days past due as on 29 February 2020.
ECLGS 4.0
focused on strengthening healthcare infrastructure during the pandemic. It covered
hospitals/nursing homes/clinics/medical colleges/ and manufacturers of liquid oxygen, oxygen cylinders
etc. Eligible entities had credit facilities with lending institutions and up to 90 days past due as on 31 March 2021.
Each phase broadened the scheme's coverage in response to evolving economic and sector-specific requirements.
From ECLGS 1.0 to 4.0, 1.19 crore guarantees
were issued, amounting to
₹3.68 lakh crore
. The schemes subsequently concluded on 31 March 2023.
Salient Features of ECLGS 5.0
ECLGS 5.0 is operational until
31 March 2027
, or until guarantees amounting to ₹2.55 lakh crore are issued, whichever is earlier. It covers
MSMEs
,
eligible non-MSME business borrowers and scheduled passenger airline companies.
Borrowers must satisfy the eligibility conditions prescribed by
NCGTC
, including account status and other applicable lending norms. Credit assistance is provided through
Scheduled Commercial Banks
,
Scheduled Urban Co-operative Banks,
Financial Institutions
and eligible
Non-Banking Financial Companies
.
MSMEs and Eligible non-MSMEs
Eligible borrowers
: The scheme is available to borrowers with
existing working capital facilities from MLIs
as on 31 March 2026. Their loan repayments should not be overdue by more than 60 days. Borrowers who have already availed additional credit under the
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Exporters (CGSE)
are not eligible for assistance under ECLGS 5.0 up to the amount already availed under CGSE.
The scheme is available to MSMEs across all sectors
. For eligible
non-MSME borrowers, certain sectors are excluded from coverage under the scheme
. These include Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), power (Generation, transmission and distribution), telecom service providers, sugar and ethanol, and information technology companies. The list also includes paper and paper products, educational institutions, and beverages (excluding tea and coffee) and tobacco. Where a borrower operates in both eligible and ineligible sectors, the lending institution determines eligibility based on the proportion of turnover generated from eligible sectors during
FY 2025–26
.
Credit guarantee coverage
: 100% guarantee for loans extended to eligible MSMEs and 90% guarantee coverage for eligible non-MSMEs
No guarantee fee
is payable by MLIs under the scheme.
Member Lending Institutions (MLIs)
are lending institutions registered under ECLGS 5.0 for extending additional credit facilities to eligible borrowers. This includes Public and Private Sector Banks, Small Finance Banks, Foreign Banks, Co-operative Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and Finance Institutions.
Additional credit support
: The scheme provides additional credit of up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26, subject to a ceiling of ₹100 crore per borrower.
Interest rate of credit
: The scheme ensures that loans are available at regulated interest rates. For MSMEs, the rate is based on EBLR, while eligible non-MSMEs are charged based on MCLR. In both cases, lending institutions may charge up to 0.75% above the benchmark, subject to an overall ceiling of 9% per annum. For loans extended by eligible NBFCs, the rate of interest shall not exceed 13% per annum.
External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR)
is the benchmark interest rate used by banks to determine floating interest rates on eligible retail and micro and small enterprise loans. The benchmark is set by Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The
marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR)
is an internal reference rate for banks fixed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). It helps banks to define the minimum interest rate on different types of loans.
Loan tenure:
The loan will have a 5-year tenure from the date of first disbursement, including a 1-year moratorium.
Scheduled Passenger Airlines
Eligibility condition
: Business enterprises in the scheduled passenger airline sector are eligible if they had outstanding fund-based and non-fund-based credit facilities from MLIs as on 31 March 2026. The credit facilities should be classified as 'Standard' (excluding SMA-2) on the same date.
Credit guarantee coverage
: A 90% credit guarantee is available for loans extended to eligible scheduled passenger airlines.
No guarantee fee
is payable by MLIs under the scheme
Additional credit support:
The scheme provides additional credit
of up to 100%, subject to a ceiling of ₹1,500 crore per borrower, based on specified eligibility conditions. Of this, any amount beyond ₹1,000 crore and up to ₹1,500 crore shall be permitted only with a proportionate amount of equity contribution from the promoters/owners.
Interest rate of credit:
The lending institution will determine the rate of interest in accordance with its Board-approved policy.
Loan tenure:
The loan will have a tenure of 7 years from the date of first disbursement, including a 2-year moratorium.
ECLGS 5.0 in Action
ECLGS 5.0 has witnessed encouraging progress since its launch. As on 20 August 2026,
6,73,979 guarantees have been issued
under the scheme. The
guaranteed amount reached ₹2,50,024 crore
. The strong uptake reflects the scheme's rapid adoption across the lending ecosystem.
MSMEs accounted for 97.3% of all guarantees issued by number
and
80.79% of the total guaranteed amount
.
Eligible borrowers can access the scheme through the
Jan Samarth Portal
(
https://www.jansamarth.in/home
).
Click here
to know how to apply on the portal.
The Government is actively promoting awareness to maximise the scheme's reach.
Phase 1: Outreach campaigns
were conducted across
9 locations between 20 May and 6 June 2026.
The campaigns were organised through State Level Bankers' Committees (SLBCs). NCGTC, PSB Alliance, banks, industry associations and enterprises participated actively.
Phase 2: Outreach is continuing across 10 additional locations, with 4 already completed
. A wide network of banks and NBFCs ensures broad geographical and sectoral coverage. MLIs continue to reach out to eligible borrowers through multiple communication channels
Sustaining Growth and Enterprise
ECLGS 5.0 reinforces India's commitment to supporting businesses during periods of global uncertainty. It strengthens access to institutional credit through government-backed guarantees. The scheme enables enterprises to continue operations, preserve employment and maintain supply chains.
By enhancing business resilience, ECLGS 5.0 contributes to sustaining India's economic growth momentum.
